newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada foreign minister to meet Asian leaders.
newsitem.headline: Canada foreign minister to meet Asian leaders.

text.p: Canada's foreign minister will visit China, Japan and Hong Kong next week to discuss relations with Hong Kong and the upcoming Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference, the government said on Tuesday.
Lloyd Axworthy will meet his Chinese counterpart, Qian Qichen, in Beijing on April 1 and other members of the Chinese government on April 2 to discuss Canada's relations with Hong Kong.
He is scheduled to visit Japan on April 3 and 4. He will meet with the foreign and defence ministers and is expected to call on Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Axworthy hopes to discuss security issues, human rights, the United Nationals and Canada's role as chair of the APEC forum, the Canadian government said. Canada will host an APEC summit in November.

"My visit to Japan will be an excellent opportunity to build on the mature relationship that exists between our two countries, through discussions on a broad range of political and security issues, including peacekeeping," Axworthy said in the statement.
He will end his trip with a visit to Hong Kong to speak with Hong Kong Governor Christopher Patten and Chief Executive Designate Tung Chee-hwa to discuss the transition to Chinese rule.
Last week, Canada announced the extension of visa-free access for most Hong Kong visitors to Canada.
